disease_label_per_paper: Persistent MRSA bacteremia with septic shock and occult gallbladder nidus after tunneled dialysis catheter source
presentation_summary: 65-year-old man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was referred from dialysis center with fever, altered mental status, and hypotension.
Admission blood cultures grew MRSA in four of four bottles; tunneled dialysis catheter tip culture confirmed the catheter as the initial source.
Despite catheter removal and therapeutic vancomycin exposure, he had 18 days of high-grade persistent MRSA bacteremia until gallbladder aspiration/drainage.
Blood cultures became negative one day after gallbladder drainage; he later transitioned to comfort-focused care and died.

all bottles growing MRSA and cultures positive <24 hours after collection
15 cc of serosanguinous drainage that later grew MRSA (vancomycin MIC 1) and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium

imaging.source_text_value: A transoesophageal echocardiogram (TOE) revealed a small vegetation on the aortic valve without other valvular abnormalities
MRI of the gangrenous toes did not show a fluid collection or abscess
Spine MRI showed possible discitis but no epidural abscesses
CT angiogram of the chest revealed a non-occlusive clot in the right internal jugular vein, which was radiographically felt to be a chronic clot
CT of the abdomen and pelvis was obtained, which showed circumferential gall bladder wall thickening and bowel oedema
subsequent indium-111-labelled white blood cell (WBC) scan showed abnormal focal uptake in the gall bladder

treatments_reported.source_text_value: started on empiric intravenous vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam
His tunnelled dialysis catheter (TDC) was removed
After 11 days of persistently MRSA-positive blood cultures ... ceftaroline was added to vancomycin for salvage therapy
His gall bladder was percutaneously aspirated, revealing 15 cc of serosanguinous drainage

outcome.source_text_value: Unfortunately, the patient's condition failed to improve, and he was transitioned to comfort care, per his wish.
